title: Advance retrenchment notification: tripartite review and how Singapore compares
asked: Ms Gho Sze Kee asked for an update on tripartite discussions about advance Mandatory Retrenchment Notification, and how Singapore's MRN framework compares with international peers.
response: Dr Tan See Leng said firms with 10 or more employees must notify MOM within five working days of telling employees about a retrenchment, and that in 2025, 77% of MRNs were submitted at least seven days before the employee's last working day. Tripartite partners are studying how to encourage earlier notification, ideally before or by the employee's last working day, so employment facilitation and outplacement support can be timely. Penalties for non-compliance are $1,000 for a first contravention and $2,000 for subsequent ones, and he said the Ministry does not see a need to raise them at this point. He added that mandating advance notification could push companies to finalise retrenchments faster and discourage backend negotiations to preserve jobs.

key_points.point: Firms with 10 or more employees must submit a mandatory retrenchment notification to MOM within five working days of notifying employees.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: firms with 10 or more employees are required to submit a mandatory retrenchment notification (MRN) to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) within five working days of notifying employees of their retrenchment

key_points.point: In 2025, 77% of MRNs were submitted at least seven days ahead of the last working day and 73% at least two weeks ahead.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: In 2025, 77% of MRNs were submitted at least seven days ahead of the employee's last working day and 73% of MRNs were submitted at least two weeks ahead.

key_points.point: As part of an ongoing review of the Employment Act, tripartite partners are studying how to encourage earlier notification by employers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: tripartite partners are studying how to encourage earlier notification by employers

key_points.point: The penalty for non-compliance is an administrative penalty of $1,000 for a first contravention and $2,000 for subsequent contraventions.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: the penalty for non-compliance is an administrative penalty of $1,000 for the first contravention and $2,000 for subsequent contraventions

key_points.point: In 2025, 80% of MRNs were submitted within the five-working-day deadline, up from 70% in 2024.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: In 2025, 80% of the MRNs were submitted within the five-working-day deadline.

key_points.point: The Ministry does not see a need to raise penalties at this point, but will review its enforcement approach and penalties regularly with tripartite partners.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: We do not see a need to raise the penalties at this point in time.

key_points.point: For the three years ending 2024, seven in 10 retrenched workers who received career coaching from Workforce Singapore and/or e2i were placed within six months.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: seven in 10 retrenched workers, who have received career coaching from both Workforce Singapore and/or the Employment and Employability Institute's (e2i's) career coaches, were actually placed within six months

key_points.point: The median time to placement averaged around three months.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: The median time to placement averaged around three months.

key_points.point: Requiring all companies to notify the Government in advance could in some cases adversely affect workers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: if we require all companies to notify the Government in advance, in some cases, that requirement could inadvertently affect our workers adversely

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay asked whether stricter penalties could be considered for employers who do not comply with the MRN requirement.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
key_points.quote: whether we can consider stricter penalties against those who do not comply

left_open: Whether advancing notification by a short period materially improves re-employment outcomes beyond earlier visibility; the Minister said the Ministry does not have the exact data requested and will check available data.
The outcome and timing of the tripartite discussions on advance notification, which the Minister said would be updated in due course.
supplementary: Whether to toughen penalties for non-compliance, whether earlier notice improves re-employment outcomes, and whether post-notification support matters more.
